title: yummy and juicy ethiopian tuna injera with tuna and shio-cure
description: a delicious and easy-to-make injera dish featuring tuna and shio-cure, perfect for a cozy evening meal. this recipe is jain-friendly and can be made in under an hour.
instructions: in a large bowl, combine 2 cups of injera flour and 1 teaspoon of active dry yeast. gradually add in 1 1/2 cups of water, mixing until a smooth batter forms.
cover the bowl with a damp cloth and let the batter rest in a warm place for 1 hour, or until it has doubled in size.
heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
add the chopped onion and grated ginger to the skillet and cook until the onion is translucent.
add the sliced shio-cure to the skillet and cook for an additional 2 minutes.
add the cooked tuna to the skillet and stir to combine with the onion and ginger mixture.
add the chili powder, cumin powder, salt, and black pepper to the skillet and stir to combine.
using a ladle, pour some of the injera batter into the skillet and tilt the skillet to evenly coat the bottom.
cook the injera for 1-2 minutes, or until the bottom is golden brown and the top is dry.
flip the injera over and cook for an additional 1-2 minutes, or until the other side is also golden brown.
repeat the process until all of the batter has been used up.
serve the tuna injera hot, garnished with additional shio-cure if desired.
